gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra X reaches its 36 kW ceiling only when up to three units are linked through Smart Home Panel 3 (or the Smart Gateway 200A); that first-generation DELTA Pro Ultra batteries and cables need an app update before they work with it; and that even this largest plug-in system is 24 kW short of a true 60 kW output.
standout_why: I compared against the cited DPU X specs page (ecoflow.com/us/delta-pro-ultra-x/specs) and the top result ecoflow.com/us/delta-pro-ultra. The specs page names Smart Home Panel 3 only in the UPS switchover line. It never says the panel is the route to running three units in parallel, and it says nothing about older batteries. The DPU page names only Smart Home Panel 2 and has no compatibility FAQ. The cited us.ecoflow.com/products/delta-pro-ultra variant pages returned HTTP 429, so I could not check them. I did not open the Bluetti EP900 flyer. ChatGPT's answer quotes 36 kW and 90 kWh but leaves out the panel each system needs, Anker's 7.6 kW single-module limit and the rule that BP3800 packs fit only the F3800 family.
decides: This confirms the DELTA Pro Ultra X as the pick for 60 kWh of storage. One inverter holds 10 × 6,144 Wh = 61.44 kWh, but the buyer must budget for Smart Home Panel 3, not the Panel 2 sold with the older DPU. Owners of an older DELTA Pro Ultra can reuse their batteries after an app update. For 60 kW of output, the ceilings in the makers' own documents rule out every plug-in system: DPU X 36 kW, DPU 21.6 kW, Anker E10 at most 10 kW per unit. That pushes the shopper to a commercial inverter such as the Sol-Ark 60K, whose battery compatibility I could not source.

findings.label: Output per inverter / max parallel output
findings.value: 12 kW 120/240 V 60 Hz per inverter; up to 36 kW with 3 parallel units
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra X Whole-Home Power | EcoFlow US
findings.note: Spec line reads '12kW, 120/240V, 60Hz; Up to 36kW in 3 parallel units.'

findings.label: Battery limits
findings.value: 6,144 Wh per pack; up to 10 packs per inverter = 61.44 kWh; 30 packs across 3 inverters = 184.32 kWh
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra X Whole-Home Power | EcoFlow US
findings.note: 60 kWh of storage needs one inverter plus 10 packs (10 × 6,144 Wh = 61,440 Wh). The manual rounds the system total to 180 kWh.

findings.label: Panel required for 3-unit parallel
findings.value: Up to three units connect to EcoFlow Smart Home Panel 3 through the power input/output port, combining up to 36 kW and 180 kWh. A single unit can connect to Smart Home Panel 3 or the EcoFlow Smart Gateway (200A).
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra X Manual (ManualsLib mirror of the EcoFlow user manual)
findings.note: Quoted from the maker's manual as hosted on ManualsLib. The manual does not mention Smart Home Panel 2.

findings.label: Older-generation battery compatibility
findings.value: The battery connection cable in the box is second-generation. 'If you use first-generation battery and cable, you need to update it in EcoFlow app.'
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra X Manual (ManualsLib mirror of the EcoFlow user manual)
findings.note: So existing DELTA Pro Ultra battery packs can move to an X inverter after a firmware update in the app.

findings.label: Generator / EV charging adapters
findings.value: Generator charging needs the EcoFlow AC Generator Charging Adapter (NEMA L14-30P to 5P8 port). The manual also lists the EcoFlow EV X-Stream Adapter (SAE J1772 to 5P8 port).
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra X Manual (ManualsLib mirror of the EcoFlow user manual)
findings.note: Neither adapter is in the box, per the manual's 'is required' wording.

findings.label: Whole-home pairing and generator limit
findings.value: The page says whole-home capability works only when the panel is paired with the DELTA Pro Ultra X. Interoperability was tested with the DPU X and with generators rated up to 12 kW. 32 circuits; switchover under 20 ms.
findings.source_title: EcoFlow Smart Home Panel 3 | EcoFlow US
findings.note: The page names no other EcoFlow power station.

findings.label: Output and capacity ceiling; panel named
findings.value: 7.2 kW per unit; 21.6 kW max with three units; 6 kWh up to 90 kWh in 15 stackable units; the page names Smart Home Panel 2 (12 circuits)
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra | EcoFlow US
findings.note: Footnote 4: generator charging needs the EcoFlow AC Generator Charging Adapter. Footnote 2: a soft starter may be needed if an air conditioner's LRA exceeds 120 A.

findings.label: B6000 module and unit limits
findings.value: Up to 5 B6000 modules (6,144 Wh each) per E10 = 30 kWh max; each Power Dock takes up to 3 E10 units = 90 kWh max; two battery circuit breakers must go inside the ATS Box when three units are connected
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX E10 Battery Module (B6000) | Anker SOLIX
findings.note: Taken from FAQ 1 and FAQ 6 and the spec table ('30kWh Max' single, '90kWh Max' triple with Power Dock).

findings.label: Output depends on module count
findings.value: 1 battery module: 7.6 kW max continuous; 2 or more modules: 10 kW max, sustained up to 90 minutes
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX E10 Battery Module (B6000) | Anker SOLIX
findings.note: From FAQ 3. ChatGPT's $3,999 starter kit has one module, so it gives 7.6 kW, not 10 kW (kit contents from ChatGPT's card title '7680-Wa…', which suggests a different module size; not verified).

findings.label: B6000 module price
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX E10 Battery Module (B6000) | Anker SOLIX
findings.note: Anker's US store price on the date read.

findings.label: BP3800 expansion compatibility
findings.value: BP3800 works only with Anker SOLIX F3800 and F3800 Plus; up to 6 BP3800 per F3800 = 26,880 Wh; the table also shows 53,760 Wh for a 12-pack configuration
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX BP3800 Expansion Battery | Anker SOLIX
findings.note: FAQ Q2 and Q3. FAQ Q4: the expansion battery cannot be used on its own. The page does not list the E10, so BP3800 and B6000 are separate ecosystems. The table does not tie the 12-pack / 53,760 Wh column to a model; it reads as two linked F3800-class units.

findings.label: Highest plug-in output vs 60 kW
findings.value: 36 kW (3 × DELTA Pro Ultra X) is the highest output among the plug-in systems found; that is 24 kW short of 60 kW
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra X Whole-Home Power | EcoFlow US
findings.note: Arithmetic: 60 − 36 = 24 kW. The other ceilings are DPU at 21.6 kW (ecoflow.com/us/delta-pro-ultra) and the E10 at 10 kW per unit (ankersolix B6000 page).

How much output drops with first-generation DPU batteries (serial numbers starting 712 / Y712) and which port they must go in: seen only in search snippets. The offgridstores and Adorama pages returned 429/403, and the manuals.plus mirror returned 403.

Current US prices for the DELTA Pro Ultra and DELTA Pro Ultra X: us.ecoflow.com returned HTTP 429 to WebFetch and to storecheck.py.
Combined output of three Anker E10 units on one Power Dock: the B6000 page gives capacity (90 kWh) but no combined power figure.
BLUETTI EP900 compatibility (B500 battery count, panel): I didn't open the flyer because I ran out of tool-call budget.
